sources.title: A Deep Dive into the MiniMax-M2-her
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Dated January 27, 2026; introduces the exact role-play model and describes agentic data synthesis and online preference learning. No production parameter count or architecture is disclosed. The alignment and RLHF sections do not explicitly identify M2 or another named base model; a training recipe alone cannot establish the nominal parameter lineage.

sources.title: Chat Model
sources.evidence: Exact M2-her API guide documents a 64 K context, text-only input, text replies, role and example-message formats, and a 2048-token output cap. This surviving guide is historical because the model list marks M2-her retired.

sources.title: MiniMax Text Chat API: M2-her OpenAPI schema
sources.evidence: Dedicated schema enumerates only M2-her. Requests support messages, stream, max_completion_tokens, temperature and top_p; responses provide text content. No reasoning, tools, tool-call responses or tool message role is defined. Its MIT metadata licenses the API specification, not model weights.

sources.title: Will M2.5-Lightning be released? Official reply about Her weights
sources.evidence: On February 13, 2026, MiniMax organization member ryanlee-dev answers an explicit M2-her local-use question: the Her series will not be open-sourced in the short term, linking the exact Her deep-dive.

sources.title: MiniMaxAI official model repository search for her
sources.evidence: Current unauthenticated official-organization model search returned an empty array. This supports the absence of a public Her weight repository but does not independently establish private release plans.

sources.title: MiniMax M2-her provider endpoints metadata
sources.evidence: Direct provider metadata lists MiniMax as provider, exact 65536 context, 2048 output, text input/output, and only max_tokens, temperature and top_p as supported parameters. Created timestamp 1769177239 is January 23, 2026; it dates the provider listing. Generic supports_tool_choice flags conflict with the supported-parameters list and are not evidence of native tool calls.

This uncorroborated recap is insufficient for verified developer lineage.

name.note: Use the developer spelling; the documented direct API identifier is M2-her. No evidence was found establishing an M2-her-preview alias as the same revision.

developer.note: Developer is identified directly by its official research and API documentation.

family.note: Retain the catalog MiniMax family key; this grouping does not imply ordinary M2 has identical weights or architecture.

release_date.note: January 23, 2026 is the public release of the tracked MiniMax M2-her API product on OpenRouter, documented by the serving platform’s own release page and exact MiniMax-provider endpoint metadata. MiniMax’s January 27 technical introduction and Puter’s January 26 integration corroborate this release sequence. Earlier Q4 2025 use in MiniMax’s consumer products is a separate deployment, not this standalone public API launch.

open_weights.note: Official response says the Her series is not being open-sourced in the short term; current official organization search finds no public Her model repository. Do not inherit ordinary M2 weight availability.

license.note: Descriptive closed-model classification based on API distribution and the explicit official non-open-source statement. No Her weight license was found; ordinary M2 licenses and the OpenAPI document MIT label do not apply to Her weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search reopened the English Her research and M2/M2.1/M2.5/M2.7/M3 cards, then checked Chinese Her research, Chinese annual disclosures, the Role-play Benchmark and M3.1-Flash. No developer-published Her total or explicit named-base relationship was found. The financial text links M2.1 to M2, not Her. Etna's collective-discussion recap asserts M2 post-training but lacks identifiable developer attribution and conflicts with the M2 card on its total. Retain null; the obstacle is unsupported lineage, not absence of an exact tensor census or hosted-deployment attestation.

active_parameters_b.note: Freshly checked the Her materials and later first-party comparisons separately for an activated-parameter count. The official Role-play Benchmark includes exact Her results but no parameter-size column; the later model-card text contains no Her reference. M2's nominal 10B active count is documented, but no credible developer statement establishes Her as its post-trained variant. The unattributed Etna recap is recorded only as a lead. No exact-model active count is established.

architecture.note: Her article explains alignment and data generation, not the production network. Ordinary M2 MoE/full-attention research and later cards do not explicitly link Her; dense, MoE and Transformer labels remain unsupported for this exact variant.

context_window.note: Retain 65536 as the exact MiniMax-provider context published by OpenRouter, consistent with the official nominal 64 K guide. The native guide does not separately resolve binary versus decimal K. This is a last-documented limit, not proof the retired endpoint works today.

modalities.note: Official FAQ explicitly limits input to text and excludes mixed text/image; the dedicated schema defines text message content and text replies.

reasoning.note: Native extended-thinking capability is absent from the complete Her-specific request/response schema and provider supported-parameters list. Agentic planning in the training pipeline is not a deployed reasoning-output feature; this flag does not claim the model cannot reason in ordinary text.

tool_call.note: The exact Her schema has no tools/tool_choice inputs, tool role or tool_calls output, and the provider supports only sampling and length controls. Generic endpoint tool-choice metadata conflicts with that list and cannot establish native tool calling.

description.value: MiniMax dialogue model optimized for role-playing and multi-turn conversations, with character and user role settings and example-dialogue prompting.
description.note: Describe documented Her behavior without asserting it shares ordinary M2 architecture or native tool-using agent capabilities.

patch.name: MiniMax-M2-her
patch.description: MiniMax dialogue model optimized for role-playing and multi-turn conversations, with character and user role settings and example-dialogue prompting.
patch.notes: MiniMax-M2-her uses the direct API ID M2-her. The public API product launched on OpenRouter on January 23, 2026 with MiniMax serving it; earlier Q4 2025 consumer-product use is distinct from this API launch. MiniMax published its technical introduction on January 27. The official model list now marks M2-her retired. Context 65536 is the last-documented MiniMax-provider limit; the native guide says 64 K. The Her API has no documented native reasoning output or tool calls. Parameter counts and architecture remain undisclosed; no developer source establishes Her’s named base. Ordinary M2 specifications and licenses are not inherited.

summary: Correct native reasoning and tool calling from true to false using the complete exact-variant schema; normalize developer spelling and describe the role-play model without importing ordinary M2 properties. Classify weights as closed/proprietary. Resolve the public API release to January 23, 2026 from the serving platform’s original release record; Q4 2025 consumer-product use is a separate deployment. October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening English evidence and checking Chinese Her research, financial disclosures, the exact Her benchmark table and later cards through M3.1-Flash. These provide no named-base link or Her count; an unattributed collective-discussion recap is insufficient to transfer M2's nominal 230B/10B. Architecture remains undisclosed. Preserve the last-documented 65536 context and text-only modalities; official retirement conflicts with surviving provider listings. The availability review reads the original dated OpenRouter release page, exact MiniMax-provider endpoint, native API guide, developer introduction and Puter integration announcement. All 13 unrelated assessments and parameter research remain unchanged.

searches: MiniMax documentation index, model/API release logs, original Her introduction, original M2.1 launch, original 2025 results
findings: Native chronological release logs do not include Her.
The original January 27 technical account describes production experience, not clearly the original model launch.
The original 2025 results place a Her update in Q4; copying January 23 provider creation or January 27 technical article would falsely remove earlier product-use evidence.
limitations: The evidence supports prior use during a quarter, not a release month; schema has no quarter precision.
An exact API-first release could be recorded separately if future native documentation distinguishes it from product deployment; no such date was verified.

evidence.release_date: OpenRouter’s original serving page explicitly labels January 23, 2026 as Released and its endpoint record connects the exact product to MiniMax. The API was also implemented by Puter on January 26, before MiniMax’s January 27 public technical introduction. Older Talkie/Xingye use does not establish a public API release.

limitations: The date records the public standalone API product release; it does not date the model’s first internal or embedded consumer deployment.
The serving platform is the primary source for this API release. MiniMax’s developer blog is dated four days later.
